title: Affine base-change charts detect divisibility modulo every power
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $t:B\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal F_2\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] whose tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] to $X\times_ST$ is short exact for every $T\to S$. Put $Y=X\times_SB$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $p:Y\to X$ and $q:Y\to B$, and put $H_i=p^*\mathcal F_i$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$, an affine open $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq q^{-1}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], and $a\in A$; write $\alpha$ for its image in $C$. Set $N_i=\Gamma(Z,H_i)$ and let $i:N_1\to N_2$, $j:N_2\to N_3$ be the section maps. Then the $H_i$ are quasi-coherent, the counits $\widetilde{N_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_i|_Z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify their sequence with the associated-sheaf sequence, and $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{i}N_2\xrightarrow{j}N_3\to0$ is short exact.

For every $n\geq0$, put $T_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(a^n))\to V\to B\to S$. Under fibre-product pasting, $Z_n=Z\times_VT_n$ is an open subscheme of $X\times_ST_n$, and canonically $Z_n=\operatorname{Spec}(C/\alpha^nC)$. The restriction of the original sequence pulled back to $X\times_ST_n$ identifies, including its two maps, with the associated-sheaf sequence of the quotient modules $N_i/\alpha^nN_i$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module, lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The identifications use $C\otimes_A A/(a^n)\cong C/\alpha^nC$, $c\otimes\bar r\mapsto\overline{cr}$, and $(C/\alpha^nC)\otimes_CN_i\cong N_i/\alpha^nN_i$, $\bar c\otimes m\mapsto\overline{cm}$. Consequently $N_1/\alpha^nN_1\to N_2/\alpha^nN_2$ is injective for every $n\geq0$; equivalently $i(y)\in\alpha^nN_2$ implies $y\in\alpha^nN_1$. No affineness of $f$ or flatness of $C$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the universal hypothesis with $T=B$. Thus the sequence $0\to H_1\to H_2\to H_3\to0$ is short exact on $Y$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. On the affine $Z$, the counits of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] give $\widetilde{N_i}\cong H_i|_Z$. Their naturality identifies both sheaf arrows with $\widetilde i$ and $\widetilde j$: on sections the counit is the map corresponding to the identity, so its square with either section map commutes.

source.place: Tag 01BG, lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent; schemes.tex Tags 01I7 and 01IB, affine adjunction

proof.text: Here is the affine exactness argument, also to be used below. For a short exact sequence of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme and an affine open $W$, the first section map is injective: a section with zero image is zero locally, hence zero. The kernel of the second section map is the sections of the sheaf image of the first map; clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identifies these with its sectionwise image. The third sheaf is the cokernel of the first arrow, and the same clause makes its section map surjective. Apply this to $Y$ and $W=Z$ to obtain $0\to N_1\to N_2\to N_3\to0$. This does not assume that sections are exact for arbitrary sheaves.

source.place: Tags 01IC, 01IB, and 01LB: affine image and cokernel sections

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$. Write $Y_V=Y\times_BV$ and $X_n=X\times_ST_n$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Y_V\times_VT_n$ with $X_n$: compatible maps to $X,V,T_n$ are precisely compatible maps to $X,T_n$, since the map to $V$ is forced by that to $T_n$. The inverse maps are the unique maps with these projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] for $V\hookrightarrow B$ and $q$, the projection $Y_V\to Y$ is an open immersion. Since $q|_Z$ factors through $V$ and $V\to B$ is a monomorphism, $Z\times_YY_V\cong Z\times_BV\cong Z$ by the universal property, so the same lemma for the open immersion $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $Y_V\to Y$ shows that the induced map $Z\to Y_V$ is an open immersion. Hence its base change $Z_n=Z\times_VT_n\hookrightarrow Y_V\times_VT_n=X_n$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. This uses no affineness of $X\to S$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Z_n=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A A/(a^n))$. The map $c\otimes\bar r\mapsto\overline{c\rho(r)}$ identifies this ring with $D=C/\alpha^nC$. Its inverse is $\bar c\mapsto c\otimes1$. It is well-defined because $\alpha^nc\otimes1=c\otimes\overline{a^n}=0$; the two compositions are identities since $c\rho(r)\otimes1=c\otimes\bar r$. The maps preserve products and units on pure tensors, and the map $C\to D$ is the quotient map. Thus these are ring isomorphisms over $C$, not just module isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 01I4 and 01JQ, affine fibre products; elementary tensor calculation

proof.text: Let $h:Z_n\to Z$ be the projection and $r:X_n\to X$ the base-change projection. On $Z_n$, the two maps to $X$ agree: $r|_{Z_n}=p\circ(Z\hookrightarrow Y)\circ h$. The composition isomorphism for pullback in [def-pc-module-pullback] therefore identifies $(r^*\mathcal F_i)|_{Z_n}$ with $h^*(H_i|_Z)$, naturally for $u$ and $v$. Pull back the counits of Step 1 and apply [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] to $C\to D$. This identifies the sequence with the associated-sheaf sequence of $D\otimes_CN_i$, with maps $1\otimes i$ and $1\otimes j$. Naturality is part of both cited statements, so it identifies the arrows as well as the three objects.

Use clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] for $R=C$ and $J=(\alpha^n)$. It gives $D\otimes_CN_i\cong N_i/\alpha^nN_i$, $\bar c\otimes m\mapsto\overline{cm}$. Its inverse sends $\bar m$ to $1\otimes m$; changing $m$ by $\alpha^nx$ changes this tensor by $\overline{\alpha^n}\otimes x=0$. For any $C$-linear $w:N_i\to N_k$, both routes from $\bar c\otimes m$ give $\overline{c w(m)}$. Thus the two arrows in Step 5 become the quotient maps induced by $i$ and $j$, exactly as asserted.

source.place: Tags 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, and 00D2, lemma-tensor-with-bimodule: quotient tensor formula

proof.text: The universal hypothesis with $T=T_n$ makes the sequence on $X_n$ short exact, and its terms are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply the affine section argument of Step 2 on the affine open $Z_n\subseteq X_n$, using [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. By Steps 5--6 and the unit isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], its section maps are the quotient maps $\bar i,\bar j$, so $\bar i$ is injective. Now $i(y)\in\alpha^nN_2$ says $\bar i(\bar y)=0$; injectivity says $\bar y=0$, equivalent to $y\in\alpha^nN_1$ by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Conversely the divisibility implication kills every class in the kernel of $\bar i$. For $n=0$, both quotients and $Z_0$ are zero or empty and the implication is tautological. No tensor functor was assumed left exact and no flatness of $C$ over $A$ was used.
